title: Completed open Cartesian identity on supplied constructible domains
statement: For a coefficient datum c, finite extension E, compactified square Q, any normalized IntegralMaps d, integral derived inputs K,L with K constructible, and all the constructible domains dom : IntegralDomains, the completed open identity IntegralEquation holds. This asserts only the equality of the actual completed arrows on already supplied domains; it asserts neither domain closure nor monoidality of the proper pullback square.

proof.text: Put V=K tensor JP and W=AK tensor J'HP. The supplied constructible domains allow the normalized open projection and exchange maps. Their isomorphisms identify the source with j'_!AV and target with j'_!W. Full faithfulness and the invertible open unit show that J' detects equality of the two arrows.

source.place: Base-change paragraph, open-factor restriction calculation, steps 5--6 of lem-sf-pf-open-base-change-square.

proof.text: Apply the beta_restriction and gamma_restriction identities of open-factor coherence. The first restriction is mu_A followed by 1 tensor sigma_P. For the second, tensor monoidality of the canonical composition square moves sigma across mu_H; its first factor cancels the inverse open unit. The restriction of gamma_j gives the remaining mu_A factor. The strict quotient augmentation normalization identifies these tensor maps with the ambient canonicalIntegralPullbackTensor arrows, so the two restrictions coincide before any finite evaluation. Restriction detection proves the equation.
